name: zerodom
description: Point an agent at an app as two logged-in users and it finds the broken access control (IDOR): same request, 200 vs 401. Plus deterministic, token-lean browser perception for AI agents. Open-core, runs local, no account.
long_description: ZeroDOM drives your real, logged-in Chrome (over MCP) as two identities, replays the same request as each, and flags the deterministic tells of broken access control — a 200-vs-401 split or a byte-identical cross-tenant response (IDOR). Under that sits a token-lean perception layer: a live page becomes a flat, uniquely-addressable interaction graph (`[03] button 'Sign In'`) with CSS selectors kept server-side — ~71% fewer tokens than an accessibility snapshot, and 99.00% of 10,756 audited selectors across 111 real sites resolve to exactly one element. Deterministic (no LLM in the parse), runs fully local with zero egress, no account or API key. Requires Playwright's Chromium once: `uvx --from zerodom playwright install chromium`.

tools.name: zerodom_parse_url
tools.description: Navigate to a URL and return its interaction graph — a compact text list like `[03] button 'Sign In'`. CSS selectors stay server-side, never entering the context window.

tools.name: zerodom_read_page
tools.description: Re-read the current page without navigating, so typed form state and scroll position survive. Use after an action changed the page.

tools.name: zerodom_find
tools.description: Search the current page's graph for nodes matching a phrase — cheaper than re-reading the whole graph when you already know what you're looking for.

tools.name: zerodom_click_node
tools.description: Click a node by id and return a diff of what changed on the page (+ appeared, - gone, ~ value changed), not the whole graph again.

tools.name: zerodom_fill_node
tools.description: Type text into a node by id and return a diff of what changed — e.g. a validation error appearing or an autocomplete list opening.

tools.name: zerodom_hidden_fields
tools.description: List hidden `<input type="hidden">` fields on the current page.

tools.name: zerodom_crawl
tools.description: BFS-walk an app's in-scope routes and return one JSONL record per page: final URL, forms, in-scope links, the XHR/fetch API calls it fired, hidden fields, and `blocked` when the route is a challenge interstitial.

tools.name: zerodom_hover
tools.description: Hover over a node and return what changed on the page.

tools.name: zerodom_press_key
tools.description: Press a key while a node is focused and return what changed.

tools.name: zerodom_upload_file
tools.description: Set a file input's value to a local file path and return what changed.

tools.name: zerodom_drag
tools.description: Drag source onto target and return what changed.

tools.name: zerodom_scroll
tools.description: Scroll the page and return what's newly visible.

tools.name: zerodom_new_tab
tools.description: Open a new tab and make it the active one — every other tool (read, click, fill, scroll) then acts on it until you zerodom_switch_tab away.

tools.name: zerodom_list_tabs
tools.description: List every open tab, marking the active one with `*`.

tools.name: zerodom_switch_tab
tools.description: Make another open tab active and return its interaction graph.

tools.name: zerodom_close_tab
tools.description: Close a tab — the active one by default.

tools.name: zerodom_screenshot
tools.description: Full-page screenshot of the active tab, saved to disk; returns the path.

tools.name: zerodom_set_viewport
tools.description: Resize the active tab's *viewport* for responsive-design testing.

tools.name: zerodom_resize_window
tools.description: Resize the real browser window (not just the page's viewport).

tools.name: zerodom_get_styles
tools.description: Computed styles and box-model dimensions for a node — for design/CSS review, not just interaction.

tools.name: zerodom_get_cookies
tools.description: List cookies visible to the active tab's origin.

tools.name: zerodom_get_storage
tools.description: List localStorage and sessionStorage keys the active tab's page holds.

tools.name: zerodom_eval_js
tools.description: Run arbitrary JavaScript in the active tab's real page context and return the result — Runtime.evaluate over the same chrome.debugger connection everything else here uses, the same power as typing into DevTools' own console.

tools.name: zerodom_network_log
tools.description: Requests/responses the active tab has made since it opened (or since this was last called with clear=True) — method or status, and URL.

tools.name: zerodom_set_scope
tools.description: Constrain the hunt to authorized targets — enforced in code, not on trust.

tools.name: zerodom_create_group
tools.description: Create a named, colored tab group the agent is sandboxed to, and make it the target for new tabs.

tools.name: zerodom_list_groups
tools.description: List the agent's named tab groups (its sandbox), as remembered across restarts.

tools.name: zerodom_use_group
tools.description: Make `name` the active group — subsequent new tabs join it.

tools.name: zerodom_close_group
tools.description: Close an agent group: ungroup its tabs and forget it.

tools.name: zerodom_adopt_group
tools.description: Hand an existing Chrome tab group (that you created yourself, by title) to the agent: it joins the agent's sandbox and becomes the active group.

tools.name: zerodom_restore_groups
tools.description: Reopen the remembered tabs of every agent group (best-effort) after a browser restart, re-grouping them under their saved name and color.

tools.name: zerodom_add_identity
tools.description: Register a second identity (e.g. user B) for cross-tenant IDOR testing.

tools.name: zerodom_replay
tools.description: Replay an HTTP request under a chosen identity — Burp Repeater for the agent.

tools.name: zerodom_compare_identities
tools.description: Fetch one URL as each identity and diff — the cross-tenant IDOR check.

tools.name: zerodom_status
tools.description: Diagnose the current connection: relay reachability, whether a browser session is attached yet, which tab is active, and the tail of the relay's own log — the single-call version of the manual WebSocket-probing and log- tailing this project's own debugging needed before this tool existed.
